headline: Fears grow of a new war between Ethiopia and Eritrea

chunks.text: Fighting {{flared up}} again on September 23, 2026, in Tigray, a region in northern Ethiopia that borders Eritrea. An [[alliance]] of seven rebel groups, including Tigray's former [[ruling party]], attacked [[federal troops]] in Tigray and nearby regions. By October 4, the rebels had left Tigray's capital city, and government forces {{moved in}}. They have since {{taken over}} more towns. The fighting has raised fears of a wider war between Ethiopia and Eritrea.

chunks.text: The new fighting has badly damaged a [[peace agreement]] from November 2022, which ended a two-year [[civil war]] between the federal government and Tigray's rebels. Researchers in Belgium [[estimate]] that about 500,000 [[civilians]] died in that war. Eritrea, a country on the Red Sea, fought on Ethiopia's side, but it was {{left out}} of the deal. Their friendship as [[allies]] later {{fell apart}} over it. They also disagree about [[landlocked]] Ethiopia's demand for [[access]] to the Red Sea.

chunks.text: Relations between the two neighbors have now {{broken down}}. On October 9, Ethiopia told the UN Security Council that Eritrean troops had entered Tigray. It called this an act of [[aggression]]. Eritrea [[denied]] sending soldiers. It said Ethiopia was using the claim as an [[excuse]] for a future attack. Eritrea has also {{cut off}} [[diplomatic ties]] with Ethiopia. Neither side's claims have been [[independently verified]].

Later, a pro-government [[militia]] and independent monitors said Eritrean troops had {{pulled back}} toward the border. Eritrea rejected those claims. Tigray's former ruling party says its forces will {{keep on}} fighting, but hundreds of former rebel fighters have {{signed up}} for a government program to return to [[civilian life]]. A German sociology professor warned that the conflict could {{spill over}} into nearby countries such as Sudan and Somalia.

mainIdea.s: New fighting in Tigray has badly damaged the deal that ended a civil war in 2022. Ethiopia and Eritrea now accuse each other of aggression, and many fear a wider war in the region.
mainIdea.why: Fighting flared up in Tigray in September 2026. Ethiopia says Eritrean troops crossed into Tigray, Eritrea denies it, and relations have broken down.

mainIdea.s: Eritrea openly admits that its army crossed into Tigray to help the rebel groups. Ethiopia has asked the UN Security Council to act, and the two neighbors are trading angry warnings.
mainIdea.why: Close, but Eritrea denies sending soldiers into Tigray. It says Ethiopia is using the claim as an excuse for a future attack.

mainIdea.s: Ethiopia has opened a huge new dam on the Nile River after years of building work. Officials say it will bring power to millions of homes, but countries farther down the river are worried.
mainIdea.why: New fighting in Tigray has damaged the 2022 peace deal. It has also raised fears of a war between Ethiopia and Eritrea.

tf.s: Fighting has flared up again in Ethiopia's Tigray region.
tf.why: Rebel groups attacked federal troops in Tigray and nearby regions in September 2026.

tf.s: Eritrea was one of the parties that signed the peace deal.
tf.why: Eritrea fought on Ethiopia's side in the war, but it was left out of the deal. Their friendship as allies later fell apart over it.

tf.s: Government forces moved in after the rebels left Tigray's capital.
tf.why: The rebels left Mekelle in early October, and government forces entered it on October 4. Since then they have taken over more towns.

tf.s: Eritrea agrees that its soldiers have entered Tigray.
tf.why: Eritrea denies sending soldiers into Tigray. It has also cut off diplomatic ties with Ethiopia.

tf.s: A top U.S. official called for calm in the conflict.
tf.why: The U.S. secretary of state asked both sides to lower tensions in a phone call with Ethiopia's prime minister.

tf.s: Experts say there is no risk of a wider war in the region.
tf.why: Many people fear a wider war, and a German sociology professor warned that the conflict could spill over into nearby countries.

lines.text: Did you see the news about Ethiopia and Eritrea?
A little. Fighting {{flared up}} in Tigray again, right?
Yes, in late September. Since then, things have gone [[from bad to worse]].
The rebels left Mekelle, the regional capital, and government forces {{moved in}}. They've {{taken over}} more towns since then.
I thought there was a peace deal in 2022.
There was, but the new fighting has badly damaged it.
And how is Eritrea part of this?
Eritrea fought on Ethiopia's side in the last war. Then their friendship {{fell apart}}.
Completely. Eritrea {{cut off}} diplomatic ties in early October.
Is it just [[a war of words]], or are there troops involved?
Ethiopia says Eritrean troops are in Tigray. Eritrea says that isn't true, so it's [[hard to tell]].
Yes. The U.S. secretary of state did, in a call with Ethiopia's prime minister.
Some experts worry the conflict could {{spill over}} into the wider region.
